evidence: STATIC DESIGN (supports a graded reward): tests/scoring.toml gates render=0.0, constraints=0.0; weights functional 0.6/polish 0.2/visual 0.2; floor functional=0.05 (byte-identical to template). score.py: reward = weighted mean when gates_passed and every floor exceeded, else 0. Functional (scored/functional/judge.toml, aggregation weighted_mean) has 44 binary criteria, weights 0.5-2.5, total 59.5; the largest single row (hro_live_board / hro_stale_refused / hro_candidate_private, 2.5) is 4.2% of functional, i.e. 2.5% of reward. Polish has 5 binary rows (weights 3,3,2,1.5,2.5 of 12). Visual has 5 likert points=5 rows with described anchors at every level, equal weight 1.2. Functional prompt.md:13 explicitly says 'score EACH criterion independently, continue after failures', 'A failed sibling verdict is not evidence against another row', 'Shared protocols reduce setup; they are not conjunctive bundles', and lets the judge re-create setup on a new job when a setup step fails; prompt.md:23 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row'. hro_refusal_status (lines 196-201) and hro_activity_refusals explicitly avoid double-deducting. So a partial app should land in the middle: e.g. a correct board app with no realtime transport loses hro_live_board 2.5, hro_msg_exchange 1.5, hro_unread_counts 2, hro_unread_scrolled_up 2, hro_seen 1.5 (~16% functional) and polish live rows 6/12, but keeps the rest; an app without multi-select loses the B cluster (hro_bulk_move 1.5, hro_bulk_all_or_none 2, hro_bulk_places 1.5, hro_undo_restores 2, plus part of undo rows) ~15-20% functional; an app with no permission enforcement loses R rows (~12%). Correlated clusters exist but each maps to a distinct product area, so no single precondition beyond the browser gate collapses the scored signal. The only all-or-nothing points are the shared-persistence gate (create job + candidate, read in an independent Observer context) and the 0.05 floor, which are intended exclusion of dead apps. WHY NOT PASS: the row asks whether the rubric actually PRODUCES a spread; that is a measured property. raw-evidence-index.json scope says verbatim 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' The only runtime evidence is a scripted golden Playwright driver (25 groups), which is not a judge run and grades no weak app. REVIEW_POLICY.md requires separate hash-bound runtime records for reward discrimination and ordering; none exist in manifest/preflight. UNMEASURED COLLAPSE RISK: the whole functional dimension (44 rows, protocols Z,S,M,L,C,B,N,T,U,K,R,V,A,D, ~19 KB prompt) runs in one batched claude-code judge with timeout=9000 inside scored budget 11100 (test.sh run_suite scored 11100). prompt.md:53 says budget exhaustion yields binary 0 per unobserved row, and if rewardkit itself is killed by `timeout 11100` test.sh `if ! run_suite scored 11100; then exit 0` leaves reward 0 for every app. Late protocols (K, R, V, A, D: hro_candidate_*, roles, hro_anonymous, hro_live_board, hro_activity, hro_restart, ~25% of functional weight) would score 0 for strong and weak apps alike if the judge runs out of time, compressing the spread toward the early-protocol rows or to a flat 0. Whether this happens is unmeasured. Many rows are long conjunctive binaries ('Fails if any condition stated above does not hold'), so judge variance on a near-golden app is also unmeasured.
counterexample: Not a demonstrated defect. Plausible unmeasured scenarios: (a) the single batched functional judge exhausts 9000 s around protocol R/V/A, so a strong app and a mediocre app both get 0 on the late ~25% of functional weight (or rewardkit exceeds the 11100 s suite budget and both get reward 0), flattening discrimination; (b) a nearly-correct app with one cosmetic deviation in a long conjunctive row (e.g. hro_activity requiring every line for every action) loses the full row, while the golden may also lose it stochastically, so the measured spread between golden and partial apps may be smaller than the static weights suggest.
suggested_fix: Measure it: run the full configured verifier on the golden and on 3-4 hash-recorded mutated weak apps (e.g. no realtime transport, no multi-card move/undo, no role enforcement, no candidate portal) and record per-dimension scores, judge durations and any NOT EXERCISED rows in a raw-evidence entry; if the functional judge approaches its budget, split or trim protocols rather than raising timeouts automatically.
